checks: Grouping a finite hull combination by base is valid because each K_p is convex. Each allowed weight vector conversely produces its entire weighted Minkowski sum in the specified fiber. Zero weights impose no choice constraint, and the feasible weight set is a nonempty compact simplex section for every z in Q. Support adds on each Minkowski sum, so the weight maximum gives the exact fiber support.

A common radius is the minimum of finitely many strictly positive input inball radii. For any feasible weights, the same displacement in all the input balls gives every point in the ball of this radius about the weighted center. Finite-dimensional compactness of the hull gives closed and bounded fibers.

In orthonormal affine coordinates of rank r the dual rows (1,p) span R^(r+1). A line direction would vanish on all the rows, so the feasible dual and its nonempty optimal face are pointed. Finite LP duality gives attainment even when z is on the relative boundary. The optimal face contains a vertex, which is also a vertex of the dual.

For every unit u, all dual vertices use some invertible (r+1)-row matrix from the same finite set, so the slopes are bounded by the maximum of finitely many operator norms times a uniform bound on the selected supports. In rank zero the base is a singleton and the slope vanishes. Active row changes with u or z do not affect the bound.

At either base, testing a minimizing dual vertex for the other base gives one direction of the support estimate. Taking the supremum over unit u yields the Hausdorff distance. The support lower bound after an error of at most R/2 gives inclusion of the closed ball of radius R/2 about y by separation.

The archived c0fc791108fc8765 digest matches the frozen provenance. Section 3, equations (6)–(8), and its last paragraph contain the exact support, slope and inradius arguments. The frozen standalone hypotheses suffice without the source's anchoring assumption.

overlap.comparison: Uses a dual affine support minorant for a minimum over representations of one fixed base and metronoid supports. That LP mechanism overlaps, but the result does not give the finite-hull support maximum or uniform Lipschitz control across real bases.

Proves qualitative Hausdorff continuity of moving proper sections of converging full-dimensional bodies in the course of its section-density argument. Proper planes exclude the projection-endpoint case, and it gives no uniform Lipschitz estimate for finite canonical fibers.

Uses additivity of support for a fixed-base Minkowski mixture of balanced cap fibers and obtains Hausdorff convergence when mixture weights approach a vertex. Here the base varies and the support maximizes over all of its representations.

readability: The rank reduction and the role of the fixed row matrix are explicit. The term 'vertex of the optimal face' is understood as a vertex of the full dual because the set is a face.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The finite-hull support formula, common positive inradius, and uniform Hausdorff Lipschitz bound hold on the whole relative base, including its boundary.
